newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Ericsson says sales can rise on own funds.
newsitem.headline: Ericsson says sales can rise on own funds.

text.p: Swedish telecoms group Ericsson said on Friday annual sales could grow between 20 and 22 percent, in a mix of crowns and dollars, without external financing.

"We can manage growth of up to 20-22 percent on our own, but if we grow more than that we will start to draw on our equity," chief executive Lars Ramqvist told the annual general meeting. Ramqvist added that Ericsson is targetting a 40 percent equity-to-assets ratio, as well as positive cash flow.

Ericsson earlier released first quarter earnings showing pre-tax profit rose 30 percent to 2.02 billion crowns, while order intake and sales rose 36 percent in crowns and about 20 percent in dollars. Equity-to-assets ratio was 38.5 percent.
Chief financial officer Carl Wilhelm Ros said growth was higher than 20 to 22 percent, but a share issue was not imminent.
"It is correct that we are currently growing at a slightly faster pace than we can manage (with company funds), but it remains to be seen what the situation will like at the year- end," he said.
Ros said Ericsson had several options if it keeps growing by more than the 20 to 22 percent range.

"If we can get good deals, we would like to take them so we don't lose market share," he said. "If that means higher growth than 20 percent, we can increase profitability, increase the turnover of capital or raise capital externally."
